q: If I ___ more time, I'd learn to play the harp.
explain: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + verb (imaginary situation).

q: The forest path ___ by the fairies every spring.
explain: Passive present simple: is + past participle.

q: She asked me where I ___.
explain: Reported questions move back a tense and use statement word order.

q: I'm used to ___ up early.
By the time we arrived, the owl ___.
explain: Past perfect for an action before another past action.

q: You ___ have told me! I would have helped.
explain: 'should have' + past participle = criticism of a past action.

q: The forest, ___ is very old, is full of secrets.
explain: Non-defining clauses (with commas) use 'which' for things, never 'that'.

q: I've been waiting here ___ two hours.
He suggested ___ the river path.
Unless you hurry, you ___ the last boat.
explain: Unless = if not → 'If you don't hurry, you will miss…'

q: She ___ be at home — her lights are on.
explain: 'must' for a logical conclusion (I'm almost sure).

q: I wish I ___ speak to animals.
explain: wish + could for abilities we don't have.

q: It's the most beautiful place I ___ visited.
We'd better ___ before it gets dark.
Neither Tom ___ Sara knew the way.
The map was ___ old that we couldn't read it.
If it ___ tomorrow, we'll have the picnic indoors.
explain: First conditional: If + present simple, will + verb.

q: The letter ___ before the queen arrived.
explain: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle.

q: He told me he ___ the dragon the day before.
explain: Reported speech: past simple → past perfect.

q: I'm thinking ___ joining the archery club.
You ___ wear a uniform, but you can if you want.
This is the village ___ my grandmother was born.
She's been learning French ___ she was six.
I'd rather ___ at home tonight.
The castle was ___ an amazing sight that we stopped to stare.
He can't afford ___ a new horse.
While I ___ through the forest, I heard a strange noise.
explain: Past continuous for the background action.

q: Do you know what time ___?
explain: Indirect questions use statement word order.

q: It ___ be Tom at the door; he's on holiday in Spain.
I'll lend you my map ___ you promise to bring it back.
